items.abstract: <jats:p>Drug discovery motivates accurate molecular property prediction when labeled data are limited and candidate spaces are vast. This article presents CardinalGraphFormer, a graph transformer that combines structured sparse attention with graph-specific structural biases and an unnormalized aggregation channel that preserves neighborhood cardinality. The model restricts attention to local shortest-path neighborhoods for efficiency, injects degree-based centrality and direct-bond edge information as biases, and augments normalized attention with a gated sum over the same support set to retain dynamic neighborhood-size signals. Pretraining unifies two self-supervised objectives: contrastive alignment of two augmented graph views and masked reconstruction of node and edge attributes. We evaluate with a matched protocol across multiple public molecular property benchmarks and compare against objective-matched transformer baselines as well as masked-modeling and contrastive baselines. Results show consistent improvements attributable to the cardinality-preserving channel and dual pretraining, alongside ablation evidence and efficiency measurements on large molecules. The work emphasizes reproducibility through shared architectures, data filtering, and split protocols, and discusses limitations tied to sparsity benefits on small graphs.</jats:p>
